issues.detail: Covers mostly happy paths; lacks guidance on diagnosing grokparsefailure, handling dead letter queue setup (the audit config comment mentions DLQ but none is configured), and troubleshooting backpressure or Elasticsearch outages.
Configs use plaintext http and ssl_enabled => false for beats and Elasticsearch; acceptable for examples but unsuitable for production without TLS and authentication.
Examples disable TLS on the beats input and use http:// Elasticsearch hosts with no credentials, which is insecure by default if copied into production.

scenarios.name: nginx-filebeat-to-elasticsearch
scenarios.rationale: A has the correct TLS options, a date filter on the right pattern, geoip, useragent, and a date-pattern index, but it names the index nginx-access-* instead of the logs-nginx example, which the rubric allows with 'such as'; B matches the logs-nginx index and the TLS options exactly, yet its date filter and geoip/useragent run on a hand-rolled grok pattern that has weaknesses, and its output is unencrypted HTTP, so A's fuller, more production-ready answer scores higher.

scenarios.name: isolate-audit-pipeline-with-persisted-queue
scenarios.rationale: A gives separate pipelines with per-pipeline workers and batch.size (nginx, app, audit), a persisted audit queue with max_bytes, and verification via _node/stats/pipelines with events in/out; B omits pipeline.batch.size entirely, though its queue config and monitoring-API verification are otherwise solid and it adds a crash test.

scenarios.name: parse-mixed-app-logs-with-grok
scenarios.rationale: A hits nearly every rubric item (the '{' branch, grok with TIMESTAMP_ISO8601/LOGLEVEL/GREEDYDATA, translate, a second grok with tag_on_failure => [], and a date filter on @timestamp), but it uses :int instead of :float for duration_ms. B uses :float and covers the same elements, but it wraps everything in an unrequested [fields][type] conditional, adds a copy-based JSON handling that is more convoluted, and its notes refer to a 'reference' that doesn't exist, which is confusing.
